## 0.6.5 (2026-11-24)


### Release Highlights

- **🚀 LoopTroop – What's new since v0.6.4**
- **1.** 🔄 AI tasks can recover unfinished background commands and pending permissions after crashes, restarts or lost OpenCode connections.
- **2.** 🛑 Background commands from previous AI tasks are stopped before new work begins, while conversation history is preserved.
- **3.** 📝 PRD revisions explain exactly which epics and stories changed and why. Invalid AI responses are easier to recover.
- **4.** 📊 Ticket reviews show the correct artifact versions, coverage reports and logs. Failed requests can be retried without losing previously loaded content.
- **5.** ✅ PRD and Beads approvals wait until the latest coverage results are available.
- **6.** 🌐 Local and self-hosted instances continue to work when the browser reports no internet connection.
- **7.** 🎨 Dialogs fit smaller screens, unsaved drafts survive startup notifications, and copy buttons sit next to content statistics.
- **8.** 🔍 Ticket search suggestions stay open when refocused, and browser Back works correctly after creating a ticket.
- **9.** 🔌 Stopping LoopTroop waits for background processes to finish cleaning up, particularly on Windows.
- **10.** 🔒 Stronger filesystem protection, safer server logs and dependency security fixes.
- ⚠️ **Upgrade note:** Node.js 24.20.0 or newer is now required.

### Summary

- Package installs now require Node.js 24.20.0 or newer.
- OpenCode tasks recover their own background command notifications and stop old task commands before handing off the worktree, while preserving conversation history.
- PRD coverage reviews show clearer item changes and explanations for the gaps each revision addresses.
- Ticket review views wait for current-attempt evidence, keep raw-output controls beside metadata, and let users retry failed artifact or log loads.
- The startup restore notice identifies saved local data, and long dialogs stay usable on short screens.
- The README demo and screenshot gallery show the current app, including manual QA, AI questions and the assistant chat.
- Security hardening: the ticket-size scan resolves containment before reading, and request-derived values on affected console logs are escaped.
- Browser Back after starting a ticket from the New Ticket dialog returns to the board again.
- CI runs once per commit instead of twice and spreads the slowest Windows tests over two machines, so pull request checks finish sooner; it also gained a workflow security audit, a shuffled-order test lane and a pre-push hook for lint and typecheck.
- Merging a pull request no longer runs CI again on code that pull request's own run already tested; a weekly full run on `main` takes its place.

### Added

- Verify audits every workflow and local action with zizmor, pinned and checksum-verified like actionlint. Any finding fails the check unless `.github/zizmor.yml`, or a comment beside the line, excuses it with a reason.
- The Ubuntu declared-floor test lane runs files and tests in a shuffled order, which catches a test that only passes, or only fails, after another one. The seed is the run id and the job summary shows the command that reproduces the order.
- `npm run dev` points git at `.githooks/` (`npm run hooks` does only that), whose pre-push hook runs `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` before every push that updates a branch. `git push --no-verify` skips it once. It does nothing in CI or in a checkout without its dependencies installed, and it changes nothing when `core.hooksPath` is already set, when `.git/hooks` holds hooks of your own, or when the folder is not the top of its own git repository. It is not an install script, so the published package carries none.
- A CI job that GitHub never gave a machine to, which has happened often since its macOS arm64 runners became scarce in November 2026, is re-run automatically, at most twice, unless a newer commit already replaced the run. Nothing that failed on its own is re-run; a gate that failed only because such a job never ran is re-run with it, and a failing advisory job (Codecov, the next-Node lane) does not stop the re-run.

### Changed

- The minimum supported Node.js is now 24.20.0, up from 24.19.0. The package engine, the launcher's version check, both install scripts and the README all require it.
- PRD revision instructions now ask for exact current and revised item titles, separate records for changed epics and stories, and a reason for each gap resolution. For resolved gaps, section-only changes can have no affected item references, while mixed changes keep affected stories; unresolved source contradictions use an empty list. Empty change lists remain accepted during coverage; the review can derive a diff from saved PRD versions, and supplied records keep their existing validation behavior.
- Raw artifact views place **Copy** beside line, character, and estimated token counts. Plain text and missing-output states use the same header layout.
- The startup restore notice explains when saved profile or project data was found, shows its local database location, and says dismissal lasts for that database.
- Long shared dialogs and the Startup Restore, Welcome Disclaimer, and Keyboard Shortcuts overlays keep their content within the viewport and scrollable.
- Startup notices stay above routed dialogs and hold them hidden instead of unmounting them, so a direct link such as Configuration opens after the notice without losing a draft typed in the meantime.
- CI runs for pull requests, pushes to `main`, weekly and on request (`gh workflow run ci.yml --ref <branch>`), no longer once more for every branch push. Each commit used to start two full runs, 86 jobs, against an account limit of 20 jobs and 5 Macs at a time, so most of a run's time was spent waiting for a machine. A newer commit still cancels a pull request's older run, but a run on `main` always finishes.
- A merge to `main` is not tested a second time when its pull request's last run already passed on the same code. A short `Merge check` job confirms that through the GitHub API: the merged code matches the pull request's last commit, nothing under `.github` changed, every job in that run passed, and its coverage report has not expired. The run then hands that report to Codecov for the merge commit and skips everything else, so it takes a minute or two instead of 13 and no longer holds the machines the next pull request is waiting for. Any other push, an API error included, gets a full run. A full run on `main` every Monday at 03:37 UTC refreshes the npm cache and the Windows test timings, and runs every test again in a new random order.
- The required Packaging check now waits on every CI job except the Codecov upload and the advisory early-warning lane, so no failing job can be merged past. It also reads every job's own result, because GitHub reports a matrix as passed when one of its legs never got a machine and was cancelled.
- A quick Linux install check runs first, and every Mac and Windows job, as well as the test matrix, waits for it, so a commit that cannot install no longer starts forty jobs that each fail at their own install.
- The 21 install and package-manager job legs are now four jobs: one per platform, with one install and one build each, and one Windows job for Chocolatey and Scoop. Every step still runs after an earlier one fails, and a failed bundle stops only the steps that use it, so a run still lists every broken install path. WinGet runs in the Windows binary job, which already has the binary.
- Each Windows test lane runs on two machines, split by the per-file times `main` recorded on its last full run, setup and imports included. The install check takes one copy of those times per run, so both halves, and a re-run of either, split the same way. A result job under the lane's usual name passes only if both halves passed and together ran every test file exactly once.
- The test suite runs once on Ubuntu with the toolchain Node, collecting coverage there; Verify no longer runs it a second time. Verify runs its remaining checks even after one fails, so one run reports every problem.
- Renovate rebases its pull requests only when they conflict with `main`. Before merging one that has fallen behind, tick the rebase box in its description.
- The early-warning lane tests the Node major after the toolchain's, its alpha or nightly builds, worked out from `.nvmrc` on each run. It had been testing Node 26 since the toolchain itself moved to Node 26.
- The Windows gate decides on Linux whether a pull request touches its files, instead of starting a Windows machine to find out. It counts only what the pull request itself changed, a renamed file by both its names, and the modules the gated code imports; a manual run always runs it.
- Four git-heavy test files build their fixture repositories once per file and copy them for each test, which cuts their git processes by 21–45%. Every fixture template switches off git's background maintenance, so a copy never races it. The shuffled-order lane has also found eight test files that passed only in file order, and each now resets the state it shares or waits for what it needs.

### Fixed

- `looptroop stop` keeps waiting for a daemon that has already recorded a pending shutdown, instead of reporting an incomplete stop moments before its cleanup finishes, and clears any ownership records a finished daemon left behind. Stopping an owned OpenCode tree on Windows can outlast the first grace period and then retry, so the extra wait covers that retry while a genuinely stuck daemon still reports the same retryable message.
- Continue handles owned background notifications, permissions already pending at reconnect or before a new prompt receipt, crash/restart history, and stream-loss recovery without accepting unrelated work.
- Completed and abandoned LoopTroop tasks have their native OpenCode tools disabled before their verified background commands are stopped, including commands with receipts older than the normal response-history window. Unconfirmed cleanup retains ownership and withholds worktree reset; active Continue sessions keep their normal permissions and all conversation history is retained. Unowned interactive callers retain control of their session lifetime.
- Coding, runtime setup, and final-test prompts run checks needed for the final outcome in the foreground, avoiding progress-only replies while those checks are still running. PRD coverage retries retain the full rejected response so valid change records can be corrected rather than recreated.
- Ticket review views wait for the active phase attempt and matching artifact/log history before showing versions or empty states. Cached artifacts and Manual QA checklists stay visible during refresh errors, with retry; PRD and Beads approval stays disabled until the first coverage result loads.
- Archived setup-plan views use a neutral label until artifact history loads and offer retry if status could not be read. Coverage progress retries reload requested log scopes and discard stale in-flight snapshots; failed first log reads are not cached as empty.
- Clearing local logs reloads requested server history so open coverage summaries do not remain stuck loading.
- PRD and Beads approval waits while coverage reports refresh, and stays blocked if that refresh fails until a retry succeeds, preventing approval against a cached report from an earlier attempt.
- Local and self-hosted API requests run even when the browser reports offline.
- After **Create & start** in the New Ticket dialog, browser Back from the new ticket returns to the board, or to whatever the dialog was opened from: Configuration, or a ticket whose list was still loading. That history entry used to be overwritten with the ticket's, so Back skipped it and left for whatever page came before it. Only an entry the app cannot show any more, a ticket deleted meanwhile, is still replaced. The new shuffled test lane found this: the existing test passed only because the entry before the board happened to be the board too.
- npm's download cache in CI is filled again. setup-node cached by itself in jobs that installed nothing, which then saved empty caches that every later job restored: macOS jobs got 1 KB and downloaded every package. Caches are now saved only on `main`, after a successful install, which also keeps the repository under GitHub's 10 GB cache limit.
- Dependency Review and the Node floor check compare a push to `main` with the commit it replaced. They compared `main` with itself, which by then is the pushed commit, and so checked nothing on push.
- An automatic re-run of a CI run that a newer commit has replaced is skipped; re-running it would have cancelled the newer run.
- Focusing the ticket search again right after leaving it keeps its project suggestions open; they used to close a moment later anyway. Its hide timer is also cancelled when the search unmounts, which was the source of an intermittent "window is not defined" error in the test suite.

### Security

- The ticket-size endpoint resolves the worktree's contained path once and uses it for the stat and the size scans, so a path cannot be checked and then read through a different spelling. Request-derived values on the affected console lines are escaped before interpolation, including logged errors, which are rendered as one escaped line.
- Fixed the workflow findings the new audit reported: a matrix value spliced into a script in `published-smoke.yml` now goes through the environment, and CI checkouts no longer keep the access token on disk. Release and repair workflows no longer restore an npm cache at all.

### Documentation

- The README demo GIF is a new 93-second recording of the current UI. It follows one finished ticket from the main implementer and council settings through the council's drafts and each model's vote scores, the interview, specs, beads, one bead's details, code changes and log, manual QA, the pull request and the assistant chat. It ends with the AI stopping to ask a question. Each step has a caption, and a glowing ring marks the part the caption is about. The GIF links to an MP4 copy on the website, which opens in the browser's video player so you can pause and scrub. At 4.6 MB the GIF is smaller than the 28-second one it replaces.
- The eight screenshots in the README and website galleries were retaken from the current UI. The two bead error screenshots now show real beads that failed and then passed on a later attempt, with the notes from each failed attempt.
